rationale: Built on the current recurrent-tail baseline instead of restarting. This run adds a compact late-phase training-loss curriculum that keeps full-sequence supervision early, then progressively downweights earlier tokens while preserving full weight on the final 128 positions. The hypothesis is that the best reverse-tail recurrent family is already strong, and the next useful budget shift is validation alignment: spend more late training signal on the tail region that matters most to final exact int8+zlib eval, without changing eval code, data paths, wallclock limits, or artifact format. The edit is compile-stable, reuses the existing masked-loss path, and stays under the line cap.
title: Late Tail-Weighted Loss Curriculum
